newsitem.title: THAILAND: Eastern Water debuts at 13 baht premium.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Water debuts at 13 baht premium.

text.p: Shares of Eastern Water Resources Development and Management Plc were trading at a 13 baht premium to their initial offer price in a debut listing on Monday, traders said.
The firm's shares were at 43.25 baht by 0350 GMT against an initial offer price of 30. The offer had been 15 times oversubscribed, brokers said.
The firm had offered 51 million shares at 30 baht in June, prior to the baht's de facto devaluation on July 2. The baht has since lost around 20 percent of its value against the dollar.
At 43 baht, initial subscribers who were selling Eastern shares would realise a gross gain of 43 percent over the offer price.
The IPO had been heavily oversubscribed by investors attracted by the firm's virtual monopoly on water supply to some of Thailand's most heavily industrialised areas.

"The demand was there before the baht weakened so it should be stronger now. I think there is both foreign and local interest and it's being helped by a good day overall on the market," said one local broker.

The composite SET Index had risen 27.33 points or 4.23 percent on Monday to 673.91, buoyed by news that the Thai government said it was talking to the IMF about a rescue package for the ailing domestic economy.
